name: Button-down collar
summary: A shirt collar whose points button to the body of the shirt, so that the collar stays down and rolls in a soft curve.
how: Sew a small buttonhole in each collar point.
Sew a button on the body of the shirt at the matching place.
Cut the collar from soft oxford cloth so that it rolls when it is buttoned.

origin.note: John Brooks sees English polo players pin their collars down, and he copies the idea for the shirt of his firm.

adoptions.via: College clothiers sell the oxford button-down as the base of the Ivy League look.
